summary: This Wikipedia-derived note gives an overview of Protestantism: its core doctrines (sola fide, sola scriptura, priesthood of all believers), its demographic spread across Europe, the Americas and the world, and its influence on social welfare, education and state churches. It also covers cross-denominational movements such as Evangelicalism, the Charismatic Movement and Pentecostalism, and historical episodes including Luther's 95 theses, the Third Great Awakening and the Scottish Reformation of 1560.
one_line: Overview of Protestantism's core beliefs, global distribution, social influence, state churches, and major historical movements from the Reformation onward.
key_facts: All Protestant denominations reject papal supremacy over the Church universal and generally deny the Roman Catholic doctrine of transubstantiation.
The 'Five solae' summarize the reformers' basic theological differences from the Roman Catholic Church of the day.
Protestants made up 12% of the EU population according to a 2012 Eurobarometer study on religiosity in the European Union.
Pew Research Center reported Protestants constituted nearly one fifth (17.8%) of Europe's Christian population in 2010.
Collectively encompassing more than 900 million adherents, Protestantism represents nearly forty percent of Christians worldwide.
Germany under Chancellor Otto von Bismarck introduced insurance programs that led the way to the welfare state, which Bismarck called 'practical Christianity'.
On 31 October 1517, Martin Luther supposedly nailed his 95 theses against the selling of indulgences at the All Saints' Castle Church in Wittenberg.
The Third Great Awakening is described as a hypothetical historical period of religious activism in American history spanning the late 1850s to the early 20th century.
Quakers, or Friends, are members of the Religious Society of Friends, whose central unifying doctrine is the priesthood of all believers.
Tuvalu has the only established church in the Reformed tradition in the world, while Tonga has an established Methodist church.
The Church of England is the officially established religious institution in England and the Mother Church of the worldwide Anglican Communion.
Luther's 1523 treatise argued that congregations had the right to elect a minister and, if necessary, vote for his dismissal.
There are over 279 million Pentecostals worldwide, and Pentecostal and Charismatic Christianity together number over 500 million adherents.
The Scottish Reformation Parliament of 1560 repudiated the pope's authority through the Papal Jurisdiction Act 1560 and forbade the celebration of the Mass.
The Puritans who established Massachusetts Bay Colony in 1628 founded Harvard College only eight years later.
